fields.flaw: Every complete lattice is an object of Frm, so CLat is a subcategory of Frm.
fields.problem:
Title: Category CLat is Subcategory of Frm

Let $\mathbf{Frm}$ denote the [[Definition:Category of Frames|category of frames]].

Let $\mathbf{CLat}$ denote the [[Definition:Category of Complete Lattices|category of complete lattices]].

Then:
:$\mathbf{CLat}$ is a [[Definition:Subcategory|subcategory]] of $\mathbf{Frm}$

0001 | From [[Complete Lattice Homomorphism is Frame Homomorphism]]:
0002 | :$\mathbf{CLat}$ consists of a [[Definition:Subcollection|subcollection]] of [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|objects]] and [[Definition:Subcollection|subcollection]] of [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] of $\mathbf{Frm}$
0003 | 
0004 | By definition of [[Definition:Category of Complete Lattices|category of complete lattices]] $\mathbf{CLat}$ and [[Definition:Category of Frames|category of frames]] $\mathbf{Frm}$:
0005 | :[[Definition:Composition of Morphisms|composition of morphisms]] in both [[Definition:Category|categories]] is standard [[Definition:Composition of Mappings|composition of mappings]]
0006 | and:
0007 | :[[Definition:Identity Morphism|identity morphisms]] in both [[Definition:Category|categories]] are [[Definition:Identity Mapping|identity mappings]]
0008 | 
0009 | It follows that $\mathbf{CLat}$ is a [[Definition:Subcategory|subcategory]] of $\mathbf{Frm}$ by definition.
0010 | {{qed}}

fields.witness: Let L={0,a,b,c,1}, ordered by 0<a,b,c<1 with a,b,c pairwise incomparable (the five-element diamond M₃). It is a complete lattice: finite joins and meets exist; distinct atoms join to 1 and meet to 0. But a ∧ (b ∨ c)=a ∧ 1=a, whereas (a ∧ b) ∨ (a ∧ c)=0 ∨ 0=0. Since a≠0, finite meet does not distribute over arbitrary join, so L is not a frame.
